title: A FRAMEWORK FOR STUDYING AI AGENT BEHAVIOR: EVIDENCE FROM CONSUMER CHOICE EXPERIMENTS
reasoning: The paper focuses on evaluating AI agents' decision-making processes in the context of consumer choice and e-commerce. It measures sensitivity to marketing 'nudges' (like social proof and scarcity) and product attributes (price and rating). It does not involve any benchmarking or evaluation related to religion, faith, theology, or formal ethics systems.
